title: Surgeon: adaptive FP8 reservoir for per-shard selection on Hopper (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Anita Verma
description:
Goal: Deliver a production-ready adaptive FP8 selection service (codename: Surgeon) that chooses between E4M3 and E5M2 profiles at shard/granularity (per-shard or per-layer where safe) for Hopper GPUs. Surgeon provides an online reservoir of calibrated profiles, runtime heuristics, and numeric safety checks so that we can enable FP8 broadly while preserving customer-facing quality and latency SLOs.

Scope:
- Offline calibration pipeline extensions to generate multi-seed per-shard profile candidates (E4M3/E5M2) and numeric heuristics.
- A lightweight runtime selector (in the serving runtime) that consults the Surgeon reservoir and per-request heuristics (sequence length, prompt fingerprint, cache-hit ratio, recent drift signals).
- Safety fabric: hysteresis, numeric sentinels (NaN/Inf counters), per-shard rollback triggers, and progressive canary gating.
- Telemetry and golden-suite validation tied to specific prompt sets: embedding drift, logprob KL, and downstream evals (summarization QA, classification AUC).
- Fallbacks to INT8/FP16 variants when thresholds are exceeded or when memory/latency constraints require it.

Why this is needed: enabling FP8 without per-shard adaptivity results in brittle accuracy regressions on heterogeneous model architectures (attention-heavy layers vs. MLP-dominated layers). Surgeon aims to provide a conservative, observable path to broaden FP8 enablement with minimal operational risk.

Out-of-scope: cross-model ensemble ensembling (future), automated retraining of quantized weights.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: silent quality regressions at tail prompts. Mitigation: run golden-suite in shadow for 2 weeks, add KL/logprob alerts and automatic rollback.
- Risk: numeric instability leading to NaNs. Mitigation: numeric sentinel counters with immediate switch to safer profile and alerting.
- Risk: latency regressions due to selector overhead. Mitigation: micro-benchmark the selector; cache selection decisions per-fingerprint; budget a 1ms p50 budget for selector logic.

Stakeholders: Runtime, Calibration infra, Eval team, Console (telemetry dashboards), Solutions engineering for early customers.
acceptance_criteria: Surgeon reservoir exposes per-shard E4M3/E5M2 candidates and a default policy that reduces token-cost by >=12% over FP16 for production workloads with <1.0% relative quality regression on monitored evals.
Runtime selector can switch profiles at request start with <1ms p50 overhead and <5ms p95 overhead.
Telemetries: per-shard KL/logprob delta, embedding cosine drift, NaN/Inf counters, OOM counts, and latency breakdowns visible in Console with 7d retention.
Canary rollout plan implemented: shadow for 2 weeks, 5% dark canary traffic for 72h, progressive ramp to 100% with automatic halting on safety gates.
Fallback works end-to-end: when sentinel > threshold, request falls back to INT8/FP16 and metric recorded in trace.
Runbook documented with playbook steps for manual rollback and postmortem template.
All code reviewed and security sign-off not required for this change (no key material).

rollout_plan: Phase 0 (shadow 2w): run Surgeon selector in shadow mode for select production models and record delta metrics; do not affect responses.
Phase 1 (dark canary 5%): apply selection for 5% of traffic with logging and automatic safety gates active; require zero critical alerts for 72h.
Phase 2 (staged ramp): 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days, pause on any gate breach and rollback to previous stage.
Phase 3 (post-ramp monitoring): 14d elevated telemetry retention and QA regression sweeps; finalize runbook notes and customer comms.
Emergency rollback: immediate toggles to force INT8/FP16 globally and disable Surgeon via feature-flag in 60s.
Postmortem: mandatory for any incident affecting >0.5% of requests or degradation >2% on main evaluation metrics.
test_plan: Unit tests for selector logic and hysteresis glue code - required
Integration tests: simulated mixed-load traffic with varying seq lengths and cache-hit ratios - required
Fuzz tests: random per-layer profile selection scanning to find numeric edgecases - required
Golden-suite: run nightly regression on four prompt sets and compare to FP16 baseline; automated alerts on >1.0% regression - required
Performance tests: p50/p95 latency microbench with selector enabled vs disabled; memory footprint measurement - required
Chaos test: kill GPU shard mid-request path and assert fallback behavior - optional but recommended
telemetry: metric.fp8_selection.count_by_profile: counter of selections per model/shard/profile
metric.fp8_numeric.sentinels: gauge for NaN/Inf occurrences per shard
metric.fp8_quality.kl_delta: distribution of KL between base FP16 and selected profile per prompt
alert.fp8_quality.degradation: fire when 1h rolling avg KL_delta > threshold or golden-suite regression >1%
event.fp8_fallback: trace event written when fallback occurs with reason tag
